readerQuestion: How should I set up Home, Away, Sleep, Guest, and Vacation modes in Home Assistant so my automations follow one understandable household state without overriding important manual choices?
selectedBecause: Reddit and Home Assistant Community discussions repeatedly ask what house modes are, whether they should be a core feature, how they differ from scenes, and how to stop presence or schedule automations from fighting Guest, Sleep, or Vacation choices. The exact-query results explain helpers generally or document one custom Vacation setup, but they do not give a small homeowner-friendly model, a clear one-dropdown-versus-separate-toggle decision, a safe precedence order, or a testing plan. Search Console was reviewed first: its high-impression query families already have assigned owner paths and belong in the refresh queue, while no house-mode query or owner path appears in the supplied export. This question is durable, applies across device brands, fits Tara's practical automation guidance, and is distinct from Tara's pages about per-device manual overrides, presence tracking, and where automations run.

candidatesConsidered.evidenceSummary: A 2026 Reddit discussion recommends Home, Away, Vacation, Awake, and Asleep as the missing household layer for ordinary users; older high-engagement Reddit and Home Assistant Community discussions independently ask for the same pattern and debate dropdowns, toggles, scenes, presence, and overlapping modes. Current search results remain fragmented between a general helper reference, community threads, and a single-purpose Vacation example.
candidatesConsidered.reason: It has recurring demand across independent communities, broad setup usefulness, a clear decision-focused result gap, strong Tara fit, and the lowest overlap with existing Tara coverage among the strongest candidates.

demandSignals.evidence: An April 2026 discussion about making Home Assistant understandable to ordinary household members recommends Home, Away, Vacation, Awake, and Asleep modes as the shared context devices and automations should follow.
A high-engagement recurring question asks why Home, Away, Guest, Night, and Day are not a core feature; replies compare input selects, derived states, scenes, and separate presence and day modes.

A Home Assistant UX research discussion asks users what home modes mean, how they differ from scenes, and how the product could make them easier; replies show recurring disagreement over one dropdown, overlapping states, and manual versus automatic changes.

A setup question asks whether Home Assistant has a built-in Away or security mode and how a homeowner should represent that shared state, demonstrating the same implementation uncertainty on a second community surface.

A Home Assistant frontend discussion shows a real input-select Home Mode implementation and asks for a clearer household-facing control than the standard dropdown, reinforcing the usability gap around the pattern.

The exact-query review surfaces community discussions, a broad helper reference, and a single-purpose Vacation build, but no concise homeowner guide that chooses a default structure and explains exceptions, precedence, recovery, and testing.

searchReview.intent: The reader wants to create a reliable shared state such as Home, Away, Sleep, Guest, or Vacation and make existing automations respect it without building an unmanageable web of helpers and rules.
searchReview.resultGap: Current results either define helpers in general, present many conflicting community designs, or document one advanced Vacation workflow. They do not directly tell a non-technical homeowner when to use one dropdown, when an overlapping toggle is necessary, how to stop automatic presence from undoing Guest or Vacation, why conditions are safer than disabling whole automations, or how to test mode changes without tying safety functions to an unverified helper.

officialSources.name: Home Assistant Input select documentation
officialSources.supports: A Dropdown helper stores one option at a time, can be changed from dashboards or automations, can be used as a trigger or condition, and restores its previous state after restart unless an initial YAML value is set.

officialSources.name: Home Assistant Input boolean documentation
officialSources.supports: A Toggle helper stores an on or off state and is explicitly suitable for flags such as Guest or Vacation mode that automations and household members can change.

officialSources.name: Home Assistant automation conditions
officialSources.supports: Conditions check current state after an automation triggers and prevent its actions from running when the required state is not true.

officialSources.name: Home Assistant Person integration
officialSources.supports: Person entities combine linked device trackers and provide home, away, and zone state that can inform an automatic household occupancy choice.

officialSources.name: Home Assistant automation troubleshooting
officialSources.supports: Automation traces and test controls help verify which trigger, condition, or action ran and diagnose a mode rule before relying on it.

existingCoverage.decision: This article owns the whole-home policy layer: defining one shared mode, separating mutually exclusive states from overlapping exceptions, ordering automatic and manual changes, and using the result as an automation condition. The manual-override article covers temporary per-device control, the automation-ownership article covers which controller should run a rule, the Person article troubleshoots presence data, and the commercial kit page retains product and setup-service intent.
